defects_found_and_fixed_during_packaging.defect: main.py relied on __file__ to locate its own directory, but Kaggle's real agent loader (kaggle_environments.agent.get_last_callable) reads submission files as text and exec()s them, where __file__ is undefined -- this would have crashed on first turn on the real Kaggle grading path (reproduced locally before fixing).
defects_found_and_fixed_during_packaging.fix: main.py now resolves its own root via sys.path[-1] (reliably the submission's own directory at that point in Kaggle's loading sequence, verified empirically), with a __file__-based fallback for non-Kaggle-exec contexts (plain `python main.py`, `import main`, test harnesses).

defects_found_and_fixed_during_packaging.defect: agents/phase3_3/expansion_detector.py's ARTIFACT_PATH is relative to the process's current working directory, not to the submission's own directory -- fragile under Kaggle's execution model where CWD is not guaranteed to be the submission root.
defects_found_and_fixed_during_packaging.fix: Added an additive, backward-compatible `artifact_path` parameter to make_intervention_agent (agents/phase3_3/adapters/intervention_agent.py) -- default None preserves 100% prior behavior for every existing caller/test (re-verified via the full regression suite and both control-reproduction gates); main.py is the only caller that passes an explicit absolute path.

defects_found_and_fixed_during_packaging.defect: This project's top-level `agents/` directory had no __init__.py (an implicit namespace package). kaggle_environments itself bundles several unrelated mini-environments with their own generically-named `agents.py` files (lux_ai_s3, lux_ai_2021, crawl, mab, rps, word_art, word_association). Reproduced locally: a cold-process `import agents.phase3_3...` resolved to kaggle_environments/envs/lux_ai_s3/agents.py instead of this project's package, crashing with 'attempted relative import with no known parent package' -- entirely dependent on unpredictable sys.path ordering from kaggle_environments' own environment-registry setup, so this would have been a real, intermittent risk on Kaggle's actual servers.
defects_found_and_fixed_during_packaging.fix: Added agents/__init__.py (empty) to make `agents` a regular package (deterministic first-match-in-sys.path resolution) and main.py now explicitly inserts its own resolved root at the FRONT of sys.path before any agents.* import, rather than relying on Kaggle's own (lower-priority, appended) sys.path entry.
defects_found_and_fixed_during_packaging.category: packaging/runtime, not strategy -- but see limitations: not independently confirmed against Kaggle's actual production servers, only against the locally-installed kaggle_environments package.

known_limitations: self_inflicted_narrow_market_price_crash (Phase 3.4): Variant D still loses 5/15 (33.3%) episodes against the expansion_oriented archetype due to a self-inflicted STRAWBERRY market-depth crash. Both remedial mechanisms tested in Phase 3.4 (diversified substitution, partial MELON retention) underperformed Variant D and were rejected. This is NOT solved by Phase 3.5 packaging work and is not claimed to be.

The three collision/path defects above were found and fixed via LOCAL reproduction of Kaggle's documented loading mechanism (kaggle_environments' installed package, exact version pinned in this environment). They were not verified against Kaggle's live production grading servers, which could in principle differ in ways not observable locally -- the first real submission result is the actual confirming evidence.

numpy's availability on Kaggle's actual grading servers was not independently confirmed (assumed present as a near-universal kaggle_environments dependency) -- AGENTS.md's documented submission process provides no requirements.txt mechanism to declare it explicitly.

The detector threshold discrepancy (module default DEFAULT_THRESHOLD=0.5 in agents/phase3_3/expansion_detector.py vs. the dev-optimal 0.3 selected by scripts/phase3_3_choose_threshold.py but never wired in) was found during this task's audit and is reported separately (not fixed here, since threshold tuning is explicitly out of scope for submission packaging) -- see the Phase 3.5 report's 'Discovered but not fixed' section. This submission uses threshold=0.5, i.e. exactly what every validated Phase 3.3/3.4 result was actually produced with -- not the never-applied 0.3.
